rules.statement: Group by what we run, never by data source. One hub per domain, with a tab per thing operated. Related operational views are not split across pages by where their data comes from (builds on one page, infrastructure on another).
rules.acceptance: every hub names a domain and each of its tabs is a thing operated in it; no two hubs show the same kind of item.

rules.title: Sections when a hub has more than about five items
rules.statement: Sections when a hub has more than about five items. The top row is Overview plus titled sections; the second row is one tab per item in the open section. The route shape is `/<hub>/<section>/<item>`. The Overview groups its cards under the same section titles in the same order.
rules.acceptance: a hub with more than five items has the two rows and the three-part route, and the Overview section titles and order equal the section tabs.

rules.title: The Overview is one card per item
rules.statement: The Overview is one card per item. A card shows a tone pill (healthy, worth a look, needs me), a one-line headline that leads with the item's live facts (versions, runners online, spend against the projection, not a bare "Healthy"), at most four detail lines, and a link to its item.
rules.acceptance: a UI test renders the Overview for a fixture of items and asserts one card per item, a tone pill on each, no card with more than four detail lines and a link on each card.

rules.title: One source of truth for counts
rules.statement: One source of truth for counts. The rail badge, the section and item tab counts and the Overview all read one server-side problem list, counted one per problem line (two failing jobs and a stale heartbeat read 3). The client applies no thresholds of its own: none on a count, an age or a duration that decides a tone reporting a problem. Work in progress shows as a spinner, never red, on any item.
rules.acceptance: repo check RC023 reports a client source that decides a problem tone, badge or severity from a count, an age or a duration compared with a number; a test asserts the badge, tab and Overview counts equal the server list, and that an item with three problem lines counts 3.

rules.title: Current state and history are different things
rules.statement: Current state and history are different things. A pipeline counts as failed only while its newest finished run on the default branch failed. Older runs fold under History, so a fixed failure never reads as current. A running build is never red, and a cancelled or superseded run never counts.
rules.acceptance: with a fake code host whose newest finished run succeeded after an earlier failure, the problem list has no item for the pipeline and the page shows the failure only under History.

rules.title: Newest first everywhere
rules.statement: Newest first everywhere. Cards are ordered by latest activity with running items on top, runs by finish time, scheduled jobs by last run.
rules.acceptance: a UI or server test with items out of order asserts the order.

rules.title: Every runnable thing has a start button in the UI
rules.statement: Every runnable thing has a start button in the UI. Pipelines (Run workflow), scheduled jobs (Run now) and maintenance tasks (a backup, a restore drill) can be started from the item. The form opens with safe defaults (dry run on), says plainly when a run will publish, and the primary button then reads "Run for real". The contract in section 3 is the server side of the button.
rules.acceptance: a UI test opens the form and asserts the dry run default and the changed button label; a server test covers each refusal of section 3.

rules.title: Name hubs for the work, not the vendor or the tool
rules.statement: Name hubs for the work, not the vendor or the tool. "Work tracking" instead of the tracker's name, "Pull requests" instead of "Reviews". The tool name stays in subtitles and links.
rules.acceptance: no hub, section or tab title is a vendor or tool name.

rules.title: Old links never break
rules.statement: Old links never break. Every renamed or moved route redirects to its new home and keeps its tab and query string. The app keeps a lock file listing every route it has ever served.
rules.acceptance: repo check RC024 reports a route in the lock file that is no longer routed (a redirect counts) and a routed path missing from the lock file; a test follows each redirect and asserts the tab and query string survive.

rules.title: A gate override is scoped, time-boxed and fails closed
rules.statement: A gate override is scoped, time-boxed and fails closed. The expiry is stored with the entry and compared on every read, and a missing, unreadable, foreign-scope or expired store means no override. It lifts only its own gate, covers only the owner's own work, and has one writer and one log, confirmed first.
rules.acceptance: repo check RC025 reports an override or bypass reader whose error handler answers yes, and a scheduled job that clears, expires or revokes an override; a test proves a missing, unreadable, foreign-scope and expired store each mean no override, and that only the gate it names is lifted.

rules.title: A card never shows a stale reason after an action
rules.statement: A card never shows a stale reason after an action. Until the next pass of whatever re-checks it, the card says what happens next (for example "freeze bypassed, the lane re-checks within 3 minutes"), never the reason the action just removed.
rules.acceptance: a UI test acts on a held card and asserts the held reason is gone and the pending next step shown until the next pass replaces it.

rules.title: Known transient failures heal themselves and never count as failures
rules.statement: Known transient failures heal themselves and never count as failures. Each known transient failure has a defined automatic recovery (a stale saved plan is re-planned at once). Only a failure that was not recovered reaches the owner or a repeat counter; real failures keep the normal path.
rules.acceptance: a test makes the known failure happen and asserts the recovery ran, a clean result clears the card and closes the repeat alert, a result with changes asks for one review, it never counts toward the repeat alert, and a real failure still takes the normal path.

rules.title: A status card shows unknown when its source is missing, stale or unreadable
rules.statement: A card that depends on a collector's status file shows unknown when the file is missing, older than its limit, unreadable or not the expected shape, and never shows in sync.
rules.acceptance: tests assert a missing, stale, unreadable and malformed file each read unknown, and a fresh well formed one reads ok (`status_source_test.py`).

rules.title: A lapsed sign-in nobody renewed is never silent
rules.statement: A collector that needs a signed-in tool keeps serving its last reading marked stale when the sign-in lapses and exits non-zero once the lapse has lasted its limit (default 240 minutes), so an alert fires.
rules.acceptance: tests assert the last reading is kept and marked stale, the exit is zero inside the limit and non-zero after it, and a returning sign-in clears the lapse (`status_source_test.py`).

rules.title: A job that stays red is raised on the board
rules.statement: A failed newest run of a watched deploy workflow on main, and a streak of failed scheduled runs of a nightly workflow, each raise one item naming the failed job. A later success closes it. Cancelled, skipped, manual and branch runs never count, and a watch that cannot be read is itself an item.
rules.acceptance: tests assert each of those cases for both watches (`run_watches_test.py`).

rules.title: A change that takes minutes to reach its destination shows its rollout where it is reviewed
rules.statement: A change that applies at once but takes minutes to reach its destination (an edge, a cache, a fleet) shows its in-flight rollout where the pull request or the apply is reviewed: what is still rolling out, how long ago the change applied, and when it is expected to land, so a reader does not test the old behaviour and call the change broken.
rules.acceptance: a test renders the in-flight state from a recent apply and shows nothing once the expected time has passed.

rules.title: One CMTrace line per event
rules.statement: Every log entry is one line in the section 1 shape, with a plain ASCII message that never contains the sequence ]LOG]!>, type 1, 2 or 3 only, and an empty file attribute.
rules.acceptance: A Pester test writes one entry per severity, reads the file back and matches each line against the section 1 pattern with the expected type code and file="".

rules.title: The logger is Write-CMTraceLog with fixed parameters
rules.statement: A script defines `function Write-CMTraceLog` copied from section 2, with the parameters Message, Severity (Information, Warning or Error), Component and LogFile, and no renamed or alternative severity names.
rules.acceptance: A Pester test finds the function, asserts its parameter names and the Severity ValidateSet, and a text check finds the exact function line.

rules.title: The logger writes through .NET and emits nothing to the pipeline
rules.statement: The logger appends with FileShare.ReadWrite through .NET calls, never Add-Content, and emits no object to the success pipeline.
rules.acceptance: A Pester test runs two writers at once against one file with no lost line, and asserts the call returns nothing.

rules.title: A failed log write never stops the script
rules.statement: The logger retries a failed write 3 times, then warns once unless $script:LogQuiet is true, and never throws. A null LogFile means logging is off and returns quietly.
rules.acceptance: A Pester test points LogFile at an unwritable path and asserts no exception, at most one warning, and none with LogQuiet set; a null LogFile returns with no output.

rules.title: Messages are ASCII
rules.statement: The logger replaces any non-ASCII character in a message with ?, and scripts put no emoji or box characters in messages. A row of = marks the header and footer.
rules.acceptance: A Pester test logs a message with non-ASCII characters and asserts the line holds ? in their place; script_lint PS001 reports no finding in the script itself.

rules.title: The log path matches the execution context
rules.statement: The log path follows the section 3 table for the account the script runs as: LOCALAPPDATA for a user, ProgramData for an unattended server task, C:\Windows\Logs\Software for SYSTEM. A script launched from a share logs to the per-user local path, never to the share or next to the script.
rules.acceptance: Review finds the path in the script matches the table row for its execution context and no log path on a share.

rules.title: The log path is declared once and its folder created with .NET
rules.statement: LogFile, LogComponent and MaxLogSizeBytes are set once at the top with a timestamped name, and the folder is created with a .NET call so -WhatIf cannot skip it. A creation failure warns and sets LogFile to null.
rules.acceptance: Review finds one declaration at the top and System.IO.Directory.CreateDirectory in a try with the null fallback.

rules.title: Unattended scripts take an optional -LogFile
rules.statement: A script that runs unattended exposes an optional -LogFile parameter so a test can point at a scratch path. An empty value turns logging off and is never an error.
rules.acceptance: A Pester test runs the script with a scratch LogFile and finds the log there, and with an empty LogFile and finds no error.

rules.title: The log starts with a header and is written continuously
rules.statement: The script writes the section 3 header block right after the folder is created (script, version, machine, log path, and the mode when it has one), then logs as it goes. Lines are never buffered and flushed at the end.
rules.acceptance: Review finds the header block after folder creation and no end-of-run flush of buffered lines.

rules.title: Per-run logs are pruned at start-up
rules.statement: Timestamped per-run logs are pruned at start-up, and a pruning failure is a warning that never fails the script.
rules.acceptance: Review finds a start-up prune with -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue limited to the housekeeping call and no throw from it.

rules.title: Fixed-name logs roll to .lo_ at a size limit
rules.statement: A fixed-name log from an unattended task sets $script:MaxLogSizeBytes, and the logger moves the full file to <name>.lo_ (one generation) and starts a new one. A script that sets no limit never rotates.
rules.acceptance: A Pester test sets a small MaxLogSizeBytes, writes past it and asserts a .lo_ file exists and the new log starts fresh.

rules.title: Severity is used as defined
rules.statement: Information is for steps, counts and decisions, Warning for something unexpected the script survived, Error for an operation that failed or an exit about to be non-zero. A failure the script handled and recovered from is a Warning, never an Error.
rules.acceptance: Review finds no Error line for a handled failure and no Information line for a failed operation.

rules.title: Log the exception message and the identifier
rules.statement: A failure line carries the identifier of the thing that failed and $_.Exception.Message, not the whole error record or a stack dump.
rules.acceptance: Review finds each failure line names the item and the exception message and logs no whole error record.

rules.title: Every swallowed external-call catch is logged
rules.statement: Every swallowed catch around an AD, Graph, device-management, WMI, CIM, MDM, SSO, file-share or registry call logs a Warning or Error.
rules.acceptance: Review finds a Write-CMTraceLog call in every catch around an external call; script_lint PS003 reports no empty catch.

rules.title: Component is a short stable noun
rules.statement: The default component is set once with $script:LogComponent from a small stable set of short nouns, passed with -Component only where a section differs. It is never left to $MyInvocation.ScriptName.
rules.acceptance: Review finds LogComponent set at the top and no use of MyInvocation.ScriptName as the component.

rules.title: Runspaces register the logger from its ScriptBlock
rules.statement: A background runspace registers Write-CMTraceLog from its ScriptBlock with New-Item Function:\, never Invoke-Expression on .Definition, and writes to the file directly. Only the display line goes through the dispatcher.
rules.acceptance: Review finds the ScriptBlock registration and no Invoke-Expression of a function definition or dispatcher-routed file write.

rules.title: Logging is not gated by -WhatIf
rules.statement: Write-CMTraceLog is never wrapped in ShouldProcess and the logger and the log folder use .NET calls, so a -WhatIf run writes the log in full.
rules.acceptance: A Pester test runs the script with -WhatIf and asserts the log file exists and holds the run's lines.

rules.title: A trial run logs the preview and its mode
rules.statement: In -WhatIf or trial mode each skipped change is logged as Information with a fixed prefix such as WhatIf: would remove ..., and the header records the mode.
rules.acceptance: A Pester test runs trial mode and asserts a prefixed Information line per skipped change and a Mode line in the header.

rules.title: Automation scripts support trial mode and set exit codes
rules.statement: An automation script supports -WhatIf (SupportsShouldProcess) or a TrialRun switch and sets explicit exit codes: 0 success, 1 unhandled failure, 3010 for reboot required, any other non-zero value documented. A partial result exits non-zero with one Error line per failed item.
rules.acceptance: A Pester test asserts the switch, the exit code of a success, a failure and a partial run, and an Error line per failed item.

rules.title: The outcome is logged before exit
rules.statement: The last line of every run is the END line with the exit code, written before exit.
rules.acceptance: A Pester test runs success and failure paths and asserts the final log line is the END line carrying the exit code returned.

rules.title: A discovery script's stdout is exactly one boolean
rules.statement: A script whose stdout a machine reads (a device-management CI discovery) returns only $true or $false, sets $script:LogQuiet = $true, and never calls Write-Warning, Write-Host, Write-Verbose, Write-Information or echo on that path.
rules.acceptance: A Pester test runs the script under powershell.exe -NoProfile -File with a valid and an unwritable -LogFile and asserts the captured stdout is exactly True or False each time.

rules.title: A discovery script silences every value-returning call
rules.statement: Every call that can return a value in a discovery script is silenced with $null =, [void] or Out-Null, and the decision is logged before the boolean is returned.
rules.acceptance: Review finds no unsilenced call and a Write-CMTraceLog decision line before the return.

rules.title: No secrets in a log message
rules.statement: A log message never holds a password, client secret, token, bearer or Authorization header, private key material, a connection string with credentials, SecureString contents or an API key. It records that authentication succeeded and the identity or thumbprint used.
rules.acceptance: Review finds no log call that interpolates a secret value, and the secrets scan finds none in the script.

rules.title: No PHI in a log message
rules.statement: A log message never holds PHI or anything that identifies a patient: names, MRNs, encounter or account numbers or dates of birth. Device names, group names, UPNs and counts are allowed.
rules.acceptance: Review finds no log call that interpolates a patient identifier.

rules.title: Log status and counts, not bodies or listings
rules.statement: A script logs the status, the identifier and the exception message of a Graph, REST or SSO call, never a whole request or response body or a URL carrying a token. It logs counts and paths, not full file contents or directory listings, and a bounded excerpt where user text may appear.
rules.acceptance: Review finds no log call that writes a whole body, a token-bearing URL, a full listing or unbounded user text.
